text: Open-Meteo Air Quality API provides hourly PM2.5 forecasts using global and regional atmospheric dispersion models including CAMS.

India Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) defines National AQI PM2.5 categories: Good (0-30 µg/m³), Satisfactory (31-60), Moderately Polluted (61-90), Poor (91-120), Very Poor (121-250), and Severe (>250 µg/m³).

source.name: CPCB / MoEFCC National Air Quality Index Launch

text: Human physiological inhalation rates vary by activity intensity: rest (~6 L/min), light (~8 L/min), moderate (~20 L/min), and heavy exertion (~40 L/min), with age-specific scaling for children and older adults.

source.name: US EPA Exposure Factors Handbook Chapter 6

text: Certified particulate respirators (such as N95 or FFP2 standards) filter fine airborne particles effectively when properly fitted to the face without air leakage around the edges.

source.name: World Health Organization Respiratory Protection & Masks Guidance

text: Portable air cleaners should be matched to room floor area using the AHAM 2/3 guideline: clean air delivery rate (Smoke CADR in CFM) should equal at least two-thirds of room area in square feet to achieve approximately 5 air changes per hour.

source.name: US EPA Air Cleaners and Air Filters in the Home

text: Do-it-yourself box fan air cleaners using MERV 13 filters provide low-cost particle filtration during smog emergencies. Fans must carry safety certifications, thermal cutoff fuses, and should not be operated unattended.

source.name: US EPA Research on DIY Air Cleaners

text: Cooking produces ultrafine particles and indoor combustion byproducts. Running an exhaust fan or range hood vented to the outside during and after cooking significantly lowers indoor exposure.

source.name: WHO Guidelines for Indoor Air Quality: Household Fuel Combustion

text: Damp dusting and wet mopping remove settled indoor particulate matter without resuspending dust into the air, whereas dry broom sweeping increases airborne particle concentrations.

source.name: US EPA Air Cleaners and Air Filters in the Home

text: Indoor burning of incense sticks (agarbatti), mosquito coils, and solid fuel emits high concentrations of fine particulate matter, carbon monoxide, and volatile organics, and should be eliminated indoors during smog episodes.

source.name: WHO Guidelines for Indoor Air Quality: Household Fuel Combustion

text: Switching from solid biomass or wood fuels to piped natural gas, LPG, or electric induction significantly decreases indoor particulate generation and household air pollution.

source.name: WHO Guidelines for Indoor Air Quality: Household Fuel Combustion

text: Switching from single-occupancy petrol vehicles to electric metro or shared public buses lowers individual transit carbon intensity and urban road-level particulate emissions.

source.name: IPCC Emission Factor Database (EFDB) for Transport & Energy

text: SaansPlan provides non-medical exposure planning only. Any symptoms such as severe breathlessness, chest tightness, wheezing, or confusion require prompt evaluation by a medical doctor or emergency services.
